cases.title: A company decided where a war could be fought
cases.what: Ukraine asked SpaceX to enable Starlink coverage as far as Sevastopol for a drone-boat attack on Russia's Black Sea Fleet. Musk refused. He confirmed it on X on 7 September 2023, after an excerpt of Walter Isaacson's biography was published, saying agreeing would have made SpaceX 'complicit in a major act of war'. Isaacson later corrected the excerpt, which had said Musk switched coverage off during the attack; Musk says coverage there was never active, so the refusal was a refusal to enable it.
cases.why: The strongest documented case of the sovereignty problem: a private owner, not the state using the network, decided whether a military operation could proceed. Whether coverage was cut or never granted, the decision sat in California.

cases.title: Switched on over a country that had not licensed it
cases.what: During the 2022 protests, after the US Treasury eased sanctions on communications services, Musk replied 'Activating Starlink…' to the US Secretary of State. Terminals were smuggled in; Musk said about three months later that close to 100 were active. Iran's parliament has since legislated prison terms for possessing or using one, and death where use is tied to espionage.
cases.why: The mirror image of India's concern: a constellation can serve users inside a state that has not authorised it, and the decision is taken by a company and a foreign government. Whether that is a freedom or a breach depends entirely on which state you are.
cases.claimant: Musk's own post; Iranian legislation as reported

cases.title: A court reached the network through its bank account
cases.what: Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered X suspended in Brazil and froze Starlink's accounts to collect X's fines. Starlink first told the regulator Anatel it would not block X, then on 3 September 2024 said it would comply. About 11 million reais were taken from a Starlink account and the freezes were lifted in mid-September.
cases.why: Shows what leverage a state has over a foreign constellation: local ground stations, local bank accounts and a regulator able to seize equipment. Brazil enforced its order because Starlink had assets inside the country.

cases.title: A drug boat navigated into Indian waters on Starlink
cases.what: The Coast Guard seized a Myanmar trawler near Barren Island carrying about 6,000 kg of methamphetamine and six Myanmar nationals. Andaman police said the crew used a Starlink Mini to navigate, the first such use they had seen, and said they would ask Starlink who bought it and where it was used. Starlink had no permission to serve India or its waters. Early reports mentioned only an Inmarsat phone on board.
cases.why: An unlicensed terminal working inside Indian jurisdiction, outside every lawful-interception channel. India's later licence conditions (terminal location on demand, Indian gateways) are aimed at exactly this.

cases.title: A dish with a Starlink logo, seized with militants' arms
cases.what: Security forces raiding Keirao Khunou seized a satellite antenna and router with arms and ammunition; the Army's Spear Corps posted photographs showing a Starlink logo. Two military officers told Reuters it was used by a militant group and likely smuggled from Myanmar. Musk replied that Starlink beams are turned off over India and were never on.
cases.why: Unresolved: the seizure is documented, the use is the officers' account, and the denial is the company's. It shows the border problem rather than proving it — a terminal bought next door and carried across.
cases.claimant: Indian Army and police; Musk's denial

cases.title: 2,500 terminals at the scam compounds
cases.what: After Myanmar's military raided KK Park and seized 30 Starlink terminals, and an AFP investigation found receivers installed en masse at the compounds, SpaceX's Lauren Dreyer said the company had disabled more than 2,500 Starlink kits near suspected scam centres. Starlink is not licensed in Myanmar.
cases.why: Two things at once: an unlicensed network ran at industrial scale for months, and the company could switch it off when it chose. Both the problem and the remedy sat with the operator.

cases.title: A whitelist to switch off the other side
cases.what: Ukraine's government adopted a whitelist with SpaceX: only verified, registered terminals keep working in Ukraine, and everything else is disconnected. Ukraine's defence ministry said Russian-used terminals had been blocked; Russian forces had been fitting strike drones with Starlink to get around electronic warfare.
cases.why: Sovereignty asserted, but through the operator: Ukraine could only deny the network to its enemy by asking the company to do it. The claimed battlefield effect is the ministry's, not independently confirmed.
